title: What If Every Parrotfish Vanished? Your Beach Would Feel It

scenes.text: What if every parrotfish vanished? Your favorite white sand beach would slowly start to shrink.
Parrotfish scrape algae off reefs with beak-like teeth, grinding up bits of coral as they feed.
A large adult can excrete over a ton of sand every single year.
In the Caribbean and Hawaii, up to 70 percent of the sand on white beaches has passed through a parrotfish.
The algae would spread, too. Parrotfish keep it from smothering corals that compete for light and space.
Beaches wouldn't vanish overnight, but the sand supply would dwindle. One fish has been quietly building the shoreline.
